moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
learningObjectives: Navigate the Testim visual editor and Test List to create, organize, and run tests.
Understand the role of the base URL and the AUT browser when recording and running a test.
Add basic validations to a recorded test so it checks outcomes, not just performs actions.
Run tests locally from the editor and from the Test List, and interpret the resulting pass/fail output.

elements.description: Testim's visual test editor has features built directly into the UI so that customizing a test — reordering steps, editing properties, adding validations — does not require writing code, while still allowing custom JavaScript steps for advanced cases (covered later in this learning path).

Each project/test has a base URL — the starting address the AUT browser opens before a recording or run begins. Getting the base URL right (and open) is a prerequisite for actions like Reassign and Improve on a target element, which need the AUT browser open at that URL to let you re-select an element.

bulletPoints: The editor is codeless-first: most editing is done through the UI, not code.
The base URL is where the AUT browser starts for both recording and running.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Running tests: editor vs. Test List

elements.description: Clicking Play in the editor's toolbar opens a new browser and runs the currently open test's actions against the AUT. This is the fastest feedback loop while actively building or editing a single test.

One or more tests can be selected in the Test List (Ctrl/Cmd-click for multiple) and run together with the Play button. Tests run this way execute locally, which is useful for quickly re-checking a batch of related tests without leaving the Test List view.

elements.text: Local runs are limited to the Chrome browser. Running on other browsers (Firefox, Safari, Edge) or in parallel requires the CLI or Scheduler rather than a plain editor/Test List run — this becomes important later in the 'Executing tests across multiple browsers' module.

bulletPoints: Editor Play = fastest loop for the single test you're currently editing.
Test List Play = run a selected batch of tests locally in one go.
Local runs are Chrome-only; other browsers need the CLI/Scheduler.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: From actions to assertions: basic validations

elements.description: A recording by itself only proves the AUT can be clicked through without crashing — it does not verify the application behaved correctly. Validation steps turn a recording into a real test by asserting specific, expected outcomes.

Validate element visible checks that an expected element is present on the page. Validate element text checks that a specific text value appears in a specified element (Testim supports Regex in the Expected Value field). Validate element not visible checks the opposite — that an element has disappeared, e.g. after closing a modal.

elements.title: Adding a validation step
items: Hover over the arrow where you want to insert the step.
Click the predefined-steps icon ('M') and choose Validations.
Pick the validation type and target the element/text to check.

bulletPoints: A recording without validations only proves 'nothing crashed', not 'the app behaved correctly'.
Validate element visible / not visible / text are the three foundational validation steps.
Element Text validation supports Regex for flexible expected-value matching.

examPitfalls.title: Shipping a test with no validation steps
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Recording a click-through flow and calling it 'done' because it runs without errors.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A test without validations only confirms the recording replays — it doesn't confirm the application produced the correct result. Add Validate element visible/text/not visible steps at the points that actually matter.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting a Test List run to cover cross-browser coverage
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming that running tests from the Test List exercises multiple browsers automatically.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Local runs (editor and Test List) are Chrome-only. Cross-browser execution requires the CLI or Scheduler, which is covered in its own module later in this path.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the purpose of a project's base URL in Testim?

options.text: It is only used for licensing and has no effect on test recording or running.
It is the starting address the AUT browser opens before recording or running a test.
It is the URL of the Testim editor itself.
It is a placeholder that must always be left blank.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what the AUT browser needs before it can record or run anything.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The base URL is the address the AUT browser opens before recording or running begins — it's a prerequisite for actions like Reassign/Improve on a target element too, since those need the AUT open at that URL.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A recorded test clicks through a checkout flow without throwing any errors, but does not confirm the order confirmation message actually appeared. What is missing?

options.text: Nothing — a test that runs without errors is complete.
A validation step, such as Validate element text, asserting the confirmation message's content.
A Reassign on the checkout button.

practiceQuiz.hint: Not crashing is not the same as being correct.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A recording without validations only proves the flow replays without crashing. A Validate element text (or element visible) step is needed to actually assert that the expected outcome — the confirmation message — appeared.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which browser(s) can a test run on when triggered locally from the Test List?

options.text: Any browser installed on the machine, selected at run time.
Whichever browser was used during recording.

practiceQuiz.hint: Cross-browser runs need a different mechanism entirely.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Local runs — whether from the editor or the Test List — are limited to Chrome. Running on other browsers requires the CLI or Scheduler, not a local Test List run.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the 'Validate element text' step let you check that 'Validate element visible' does not?

options.text: Whether the element exists in the DOM at all.
That a specific text value appears within the specified element, optionally matched with Regex.
Whether the element has disappeared from the page.

practiceQuiz.hint: Visible checks presence; Text checks presence AND content.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Validate element text is like Validate element visible but additionally checks that a specific text value appears in the element, and Testim supports Regex in the Expected Value field for flexible matching.

quickRecap.value: Where the AUT browser starts for recording and running — a prerequisite for Reassign/Improve too.
Fastest feedback loop for the single test currently open.
Run a selected batch of tests locally in one go (Ctrl/Cmd-click to multi-select).
Chrome only — cross-browser needs CLI or Scheduler.
Validate element visible / not visible / text — turn a recording into an actual assertion-based test.
